question: I'm a non-EU graduate in France on a 'recherche d'emploi/création d'entreprise' card. I've been offered a salaried job in Paris whose subject only loosely relates to my master's degree, and the salary is below €2,800.53 gross. Does my employer need to request a work authorization, and can I take the job on this card?
reference_answer: The card allows salaried work without the employer having to request a work authorization. However, the job must necessarily correspond to your training or research, and the pay must be above €2,800.53. A job that only loosely matches your degree and pays less than €2,800.53 fails the pay condition and probably the training-match condition, so this card does not cover it. The 60% limit does not apply to this card.

question: I hold a long-term resident-EU card issued by Portugal and have just moved to Paris for a job at a French company. Can I start working right away on this card? What deadline do I have, and what might my employer still have to do afterwards?
reference_answer: No. A long-term resident-EU card obtained in another EU country does not allow work in France. You must apply for a French residence permit no later than 3 months after entering France. Depending on the permit you obtain, your employer may then need to request a work authorization.

question: I'm a non-EU national registered as a jobseeker with France Travail, and a Paris employer wants to hire me quickly. Must the employer check my residence permit with the prefecture at least 2 working days before my start date? And if the check were required and the prefecture never replied, would the employer be in breach?
reference_answer: Normally the employer must verify the authenticity of the work-authorizing residence permit with the prefecture of the place of hiring at least 2 working days before the hire. But this check does not have to be done if the foreign national is registered on the France Travail jobseeker list, which applies to you. In any case, if the prefecture does not reply within 2 working days of receiving the request, the employer's verification obligation is considered fulfilled, so silence would not put the employer in breach.

question: I'm a non-EU student in Paris with a VLS-TS or 'étudiant' card and want a salaried part-time job. What cap applies to my work without work authorization, and what must the employer do and by when before hiring me?
reference_answer: The card lets you work as an employee without a work authorization for a maximum of 60% of annual working time, which is 964 hours. The employer must make a nominative declaration to the prefecture 2 working days before the hiring date.

question: My partner is a Spanish citizen who will work in Paris, and I am a non-EEA national who will accompany them. Does my partner need a residence permit, and what about me?
reference_answer: Your partner, as a citizen of an EEA country, is not obliged to hold a residence permit, though they may request one. You, as an accompanying family member of foreign nationality other than EEA or Swiss, must hold a card: either the 'Membre de la famille d'un citoyen de l'Union/EEE/Suisse' residence card or the 'Séjour permanent - Toutes activités professionnelles' card.

question: I'm 25, a non-EU employee who just signed a permanent work contract and will move to Paris. I want to share a flat with one other person, and we want to use Visale. Is there a deadline to apply after I was hired, and how are our resources counted? What if a third flatmate joined us?
reference_answer: Visale is open to tenants from 17 years and 10 months up to under 26, and employees are included, so a 25-year-old employee can qualify under conditions. With a current work contract, you must apply for Visale within 6 months of being hired (or alternatively within 6 months of a transfer, or meet the stated maximum monthly net salary condition). For 2 flatmates on the same visa, the resources of both are counted to calculate the maximum rent. With 3 or more flatmates, each must submit an individual visa application and declare their own resources to calculate their own maximum rent.
quotes: Tous les locataires âgés d’au moins 17 ans et 10 mois, jusqu’à moins de 26 ans (étudiant, alternant, fonctionnaire, salarié, sans emploi...), peuvent obtenir la garantie Visale, sous certaines conditions.

Dans ce cas, les ressources des 2 colocataires sont pris en compte pour calculer le maximum du loyer.
Chaque colocataire doit faire une demande individuelle de visa, en renseignant ses propres ressources pour le calcul de son loyer maximum.

question: I'm 24 and on a normal (non-seasonal) work contract. I found a Paris flat at 2,100 € a month including charges, and my resources are very high, so the 'half of resources' rule is fine for me. Can I still get Visale? And if I did get it and later missed rent, would I owe anything?
reference_answer: Not for this flat. For a non-seasonal tenant under 26, the rent must not exceed half of the total resources taken into account, with a maximum of 1940 € including charges. When the rent exceeds that maximum, the Visale guarantee is not granted, so 2,100 € would be refused even with high resources. In general, if Visale applies and rent is unpaid or the property is damaged, Action Logement pays the landlord first and then recovers the amount from the tenant, so the tenant must reimburse it.

question: I'm 23 and have a promise of hire from a Paris employer, starting in 2 months, but no contract yet. The landlord is my uncle. Can I use Visale, and what must I do to get and use the visa?
reference_answer: Probably not with this landlord: the tenant and landlord must not be members of the same family (grandparent, parent or child). An uncle is not in that list, so this specific exclusion would not apply, but the other conditions still do. The wording about a promise of hire with start of duties within 3 months appears under the seasonal worker conditions; a 2-month start would fit that timing. The tenant must create a personal account on Visale.fr before the lease is signed, Action Logement checks the conditions and sends the visa within a few working days, and the tenant must hand the visa to the future landlord, who must accept the guarantee deed. The guarantee is free.

question: I'm moving to Paris on a seasonal contract and want Visale. What exactly must I show regarding my employment, and what happens if the job hasn't started yet?
reference_answer: A seasonal worker must either have a current work contract marked 'saisonnier', or have a promise of hire with start of duties within 3 months. The documents are the seasonal employment contract or the promise of hire. The applicant must also create a personal account on Visale.fr before the lease is signed, and hand the visa obtained to the future landlord.

question: I'm building my rental application on DossierFacile for a Paris flat. A landlord's agency asks me for extra documents beyond the basics. What documents does DossierFacile ask for, and how is the file shared with the agency?
reference_answer: DossierFacile asks for the necessary documents and only those: an identity document, proof of housing situation, proof of professional situation, tax notice (avis d'imposition) and proof of income. The tenant uploads these and then shares the file with landlords and agencies through secure links that expire.

question: I'm a non-EU employee who has just moved to Paris. A bank designated by the Banque de France opened my account under the right to an account. In one month, 6 of my operations were executed with insufficient funds, and the bank charged an intervention commission on each. What is the most I can be charged for those commissions that month, and can the bank also charge me for opening the account or for using the basic services?
reference_answer: Opening the account and using the basic banking services are free. The intervention commissions for right-to-account beneficiaries are capped at 4 € per operation and 20 € per month. Six operations at the 4 € maximum would come to 24 €, so the monthly cap applies and the total is at most 20 €.
quotes: L'ouverture d'un compte bancaire dans le cadre du droit au compte et l'utilisation des services bancaires de base sont gratuits.
Pour les bénéficiaires du droit au compte, les commissions perçues sont plafonnées à 4 € par opération dans la limite de 20 € par mois.

question: With my right-to-account account, I had 2 overdrawn operations in March and 7 in April, and each was charged the maximum per-operation commission. How much could the bank charge me in each of the two months at most?
reference_answer: In March, 2 operations at 4 € each come to 8 €, which is under the monthly limit. In April, 7 operations at 4 € would be 28 €, but the commissions are capped at 20 € for the month. The cap is 4 € per operation and 20 € per month.
quotes: Pour les bénéficiaires du droit au compte, les commissions perçues sont plafonnées à 4 € par opération dans la limite de 20 € par mois.

question: My work contract in Paris ended and I no longer meet the domicile or residence conditions. The bank that holds my right-to-account account says it will close the account. Can it do this on its own? What must it send me and whom must it inform? Do I get a notice period?
reference_answer: Yes. The bank designated by the Banque de France can decide alone to close the account if one of the listed conditions is met, and no longer meeting the domicile or residence conditions is one of them. The bank must send you its reasoned decision by post and inform the Banque de France. You have 2 months' notice. That notice period does not apply only if you deliberately used the account for illegal operations or gave inaccurate information.

question: The bank says it found that I gave inaccurate information when opening my right-to-account account, and that it is closing the account. Am I still entitled to the 2-month notice? Is the bank still bound by any formalities?
reference_answer: No. The 2-month notice does not apply where inaccurate information was provided, or where the account was deliberately used for illegal operations. The bank still has to send you its reasoned decision by post and inform the Banque de France.
quotes: Vous disposez d'un délai de 2 mois de préavis sauf dans les 2 cas suivants :

question: I opened my account in Paris under the right to an account. Does my account agreement cover whatever services I want, and which charges are free? If I overdraw it, are the commissions also free?
reference_answer: No. The account agreement is limited to the basic banking services, such as account opening, maintenance and closure, bank details, SEPA payments, a bank card and cash deposits and withdrawals. Opening the account and using these basic services are free. The commissions for operations executed with insufficient funds are not free: they are capped at 4 € per operation and 20 € per month.

question: I'm a non-EU national arriving in Paris on a Passeport Talent - salarié permit, and my spouse and child are joining me. Which health insurance office should I deal with for my affiliation and for any work accident claim, and from when are my spouse and child covered by French Assurance Maladie?
reference_answer: As a Passeport Talent - salarié holder residing in France, you must deal with the CPAM de Paris for all your procedures, including your affiliation request, reimbursement of health costs and handling of work accidents. Your spouse and child are covered by the French Assurance Maladie, with benefits in kind, once they have resided in France with you for more than 3 months.

question: I've just started a salaried job in Paris and I'm worried about being covered if I get hurt at work in my first weeks, since I haven't worked long enough in France. Do I need a minimum amount of work to be reimbursed for medical costs or covered for a work accident, and does the same apply to sick-pay-type cash benefits?
reference_answer: No minimum activity is needed for reimbursement of health costs: as an employee, your professional activity alone entitles you to reimbursement for illness or maternity, and employees no longer have to prove a minimum activity. Work accident and occupational disease insurance (AT/MP) applies from hiring with no eligibility conditions. Cash benefits (sickness, maternity, disability, death) are different: they require certain conditions, notably a minimum work duration or a minimum contribution amount.
quotes: Les salariés n'ont plus à justifier d'une activité minimale.
Vous bénéficiez de l'assurance accidents du travail - maladies professionnelles (AT/MP) dès votre embauche, sans conditions d'ouverture de droit à remplir.

Sous réserve de remplir certaines conditions, notamment justifier d'une durée de travail minimum ou d'un montant de cotisations minimum, vous pouvez également bénéficier des prestations en espèces des assurances maladie, maternité, invalidité et décès.

question: I worked for years in my home country's insurance system before moving to Paris as an employee. I want those earlier insurance periods counted when French health insurance opens my rights, and I also may want French Assurance Maladie to reimburse care I receive back home. What forms do I need, and from whom or to whom do they go?
reference_answer: To have your insurance, employment or residence periods in your home country taken into account, ask your home country's health insurance fund for form S041 (Attestation concernant la totalisation des périodes d'assurance, d'emploi ou de résidence). For reimbursement of care received in your home country, if you choose to be reimbursed by French Assurance Maladie, send the paid invoices and proofs of payment with form S3125 (Soins reçus à l'étranger) to your health insurance fund in France. Reimbursement is based on French social security rates and limited to the expenses actually incurred.

question: I'm an employee who will live in Paris. Which insurance fund will I be affiliated with automatically, and would that change if I were instead living in Guadeloupe or Mayotte? Also, would a foreign language assistant in Paris go to the same fund as me?
reference_answer: As an employee you are compulsorily attached to the general social security scheme and affiliated with the health insurance fund of your place of residence: the CPAM in metropolitan France (so Paris), the CGSS in the overseas departments (Guadeloupe, Martinique, Guyane, La Réunion), or the CSSM in Mayotte. Foreign language assistants (like Passeport Talent - salarié holders, foreign models and au pairs) residing in France must deal with the CPAM de Paris for all their procedures.
quotes: En tant que salarié, vous êtes obligatoirement rattaché au régime général de sécurité sociale et vous êtes affilié à la caisse d'Assurance Maladie de votre lieu de résidence : caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM) en métropole, caisse générale de sécurité sociale (CGSS) dans les départements d'outre-mer (Guadeloupe, Martinique, Guyane, la Réunion) ou caisse de sécurité sociale de Mayotte (CSSM) à Mayotte.

question: My colleague is an EU/EEE national who works for our Paris-based company but keeps living in their home country. How can their medical care there be covered, which form is needed, where do they request it and where does it go? Does it matter that I, a non-EU employee living in Paris, am in a different situation?
reference_answer: Because your colleague is a resident of an EU/EEE country who continues to live there while working in France, they can use the S1 form to have care in their country of residence covered. They request it from the CPAM of the location of their company's head office in France (here, Paris) and send it to the competent body in their state of residence. This differs from your situation: as a non-EU employee living in France, you are affiliated to the CPAM of your place of residence under the general scheme.
quotes: Demandez-le à la CPAM du lieu du siège social de votre entreprise en France envoyez-le à l’organisme compétent dans votre État de résidence.

En tant que salarié, vous êtes obligatoirement rattaché au régime général de sécurité sociale et vous êtes affilié à la caisse d'Assurance Maladie de votre lieu de résidence : caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM) en métropole, caisse générale de sécurité sociale (CGSS) dans les départements d'outre-mer (Guadeloupe, Martinique, Guyane, la Réunion) ou caisse de sécurité sociale de Mayotte (CSSM) à Mayotte.
